name: Émile Gallé
summary: 19th-century French designer and manufacturer known for works in glass, wood, and ceramics.

name: Charles Gallé
summary: Father of Émile Gallé, a porcelain painter and manufacturer.

name: Fanny Reinemer
summary: Mother of Émile Gallé, daughter of a ceramics and glassware shop owner.

name: Victor Prouvé
summary: French painter and sculptor who collaborated with Gallé on designs.

name: Louis Hestaux
summary: Head of Gallé's design studio and collaborator on works like Le Rhin.

name: Nancy
summary: City in the province of Lorraine, France, where Gallé was born and worked.

name: France
summary: Nation where Gallé lived and worked.

name: Germany
summary: Neighboring nation and economic rival to France during Gallé's career.

name: Gallé-Reinemer
summary: Family business manufacturing glass and porcelain, later managed by Émile Gallé.

name: École de Nancy
summary: Regional group of artists and industrialists founded by Gallé.

name: Le Rhin
summary: Monumental marquetry table created by Gallé for the Exposition universelle of 1889.

name: Lycée impérial
summary: Secondary school in Nancy where Gallé studied beginning in 1858.

name: Académie de Nancy
summary: Art academy in Nancy where Gallé studied starting in 1865.
